voiceover:
[conversational] Stop using ChatGPT for everything. Seriously.

ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity all have a free plan, and each might win a different job. So don't trust me. Test them.

Open chatgpt.com, claude.ai, gemini.google.com and perplexity.ai in 4 tabs. Paste the exact same prompt in each. For research, try: [playful] Explain how electric cars work in 5 bullet points with sources.

Then score each answer from 1 to 5. Are sources shown? Is it correct? For coding, does the code run? For long writing, paste the same long document in all 4 and see which hits a limit first.

[whispers] Perplexity shows numbered sources, so watch it on research.

[serious] Honest catch: every free plan has caps, and they change often. Claude and Gemini don't publish a fixed message count.

Which one wins coding for you?

Send this to the friend who opens ChatGPT for everything.

topic: ChatGPT isn't the best AI for every job. Show which free AI tool to use for research, long writing, coding and content, and a quick test to compare them on the same prompt.

pick.topic: ChatGPT isn't the best AI for every job. Show which free AI tool to use for research, long writing, coding and content, and a quick test to compare them on the same prompt.
pick.tool: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini vs Perplexity (free tiers)
pick.angle: Stop using ChatGPT for everything: 4 jobs where a free AI does it better
pick.why: 1.41M views and 3,895 comments, a very high comment-to-view ratio for a 'ChatGPT isn't the best' claim, which people argue about. It's a safe contrarian angle that's easy to check. It's teachable in 3 steps (task, best tool, one example prompt) and uses only free tools.

research.tool: ChatGPT Free vs Claude Free vs Gemini Free vs Perplexity Free (side-by-side test on the same prompt)
research.availability: All four have a permanent $0 plan on web and phone apps. All have usage caps. Ads on ChatGPT Free are reported in the US since Feb 2026 and in Taiwan since Sep 2026, per third-party sources. Free-tier limits have changed several times in 2026, so show no hard numbers on screen without re-checking the day you publish.
steps: Pick ONE test prompt and paste the identical text into all four (e.g. 'Explain [topic] in 5 bullet points with sources' for research; 'Write a 300-word [type] in a friendly tone' for writing; 'Write a Python script that renames files by date, with comments' for coding; 'Give me 5 Instagram Reel hooks for [niche]' for content).
Open chatgpt.com, claude.ai, gemini.google.com and perplexity.ai in four browser tabs (or the four phone apps), signed in on the free plan.
Start a new chat in each, paste the same prompt, and send it.
Compare for each result: (a) are sources/citations shown, (b) how complete or correct is the answer, (c) tone and writing quality, (d) does the code run, (e) speed.
Score each tool 1–5 per job and pick a 'default' per job. For the 'long writing' job, paste the same long document in all four to see which one hits a limit first.
facts: <cite index="39-3,39-4">OpenAI removed limits on text-based chats for all ChatGPT users on Aug 6, 2026; GPT-5.6 Luna became the default for Free and Go.</cite>

<cite index="41-7,41-8">Free and Go users get unlimited text chats (subject to abuse guardrails) and a Think button for harder questions; limits still apply to file uploads, images and other tools (OpenAI release notes, Aug 6, 2026).</cite>

<cite index="41-4,41-5">OpenAI release notes Oct 7, 2026: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI roll out; Free and Go use GPT-6 Luna, while Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise use GPT-6 Sol.</cite> Say 'ChatGPT free' rather than a model name, because names are changing fast.
<cite index="4-2">Free ChatGPT users are limited to 3 file uploads per day (quoted from OpenAI's help text via a third-party tracker).</cite>
<cite index="12-3,12-4">Claude Free has a session-based usage limit that resets every five hours, and the number of messages varies with demand (Anthropic help center).</cite>
<cite index="19-5">Claude Free currently includes Sonnet and Haiku, a 200K context window and up to five Projects (third-party, Oct 2026).</cite>
<cite index="14-3">Anthropic publishes no fixed message count. Pro gives at least 5x Free's usage per session.</cite>

<cite index="15-6">Per a third-party plan guide, Claude Code and Claude in Chrome are not on Free, but Claude Design, Slides and Docs are.</cite> Treat this as unverified until checked on claude.com/pricing.

<cite index="26-4">Free Gemini has standard limits and a 32K-token context window. It includes image generation, Deep Research, Gemini Live, Canvas and Gems, and refreshes every 5 hours until a weekly limit.</cite>
<cite index="26-1">Google AI Plus ($4.99) gets 2x the free limits, AI Pro ($19.99) gets 4x.</cite>
<cite index="49-2">Google's 1M-token window is described as up to 1,500 pages of text or 30,000 lines of code, and the free 32K window is about 3% of that.</cite>
<cite index="22-5">Gemini shows your usage on its Usage limits page, opened from Settings at the bottom left of gemini.google.com.</cite>

<cite index="35-2">Perplexity Free gives practically unlimited basic searches with citations, 3 Pro Searches a day and 1 Deep Research query a month.</cite> <cite index="35-7">This is lower than the 5 Pro Searches per day that many older guides still quote.</cite>
<cite index="38-4">Perplexity Free has no model choice (Perplexity picks the model) and no Comet Assistant agent tasks.</cite>

Prices of the paid tiers: ChatGPT Plus $20/month, Claude Pro $20/month ($17 billed annually), Google AI Pro $19.99, Perplexity Pro $20. Sources are third-party and the Claude and Perplexity ones are in the list above.
do_not_claim: 'Gemini Pro free with the longest memory: throw in an hour of video or a whole company codebase and it won't forget a letter'. The free Gemini app has a 32K-token context window (about 48 pages). The 1M-token window is on Google AI Pro/Ultra, which are paid.

'ChatGPT makes you pay for subscriptions to analyze files and forgets the start after a few questions'. ChatGPT Free now has unlimited text chats and file uploads on the free plan (capped at 3/day per third-party reports). Free ChatGPT does have a smaller context window (reported as ~16K / ~12 pages), so 'forgets in long chats' is partly true but should not be exaggerated.
'Gemini is free with no limits' or 'all free, no payment' for every tool. Every free tier is capped (5-hour windows, weekly caps, daily Pro searches).
Any fixed number of free messages per day for Claude or Gemini. Neither company publishes one.
'5 Pro searches/day free on Perplexity'. The current figure is 3 per day, with 1 Deep Research per month. Older guides say 5.

Unverified: Qwen making images, video and presentations for free; NotebookLM, Luma/'Lumā', Kling ('كلي'), HeyGen and n8n claims (image-to-video quality, finding leads, talking-face videos, automation while you sleep). None were checked, and several are probably paid or credit-limited. Keep them out of a 4-tool reel.
Calling Claude/Gemini/Perplexity 'better than ChatGPT' as a fact. No source verifies it. Frame it as 'try them on your own prompt'.
The reel is a funnel for the creator's links (comment 'AI'). Treat it as promotional. One top comment says 'Gemini is stupid', which shows results vary.
criticism: Free tiers are volatile. Gemini cut free Gemini 3 Pro access to 'Basic access' within days of launch because of demand (<cite index="20-6,20-7">9to5Google, Nov 2025</cite>). Perplexity's free Pro Search cap fell from 5 to 3 per day.
Claude Free and Gemini Free give no fixed message count, so you can hit a limit unpredictably. <cite index="11-6">Claude Free's message count 'will vary based on demand'.</cite>

Free Gemini's small 32K context hurts long-document work. A third-party source says Google may use what you send on the free API tier to improve its products. That is the API, not the app, so don't blur the two.
ChatGPT Free by default can use conversations to train models unless you opt out in settings (third-party source), and ads are shown to free users in some countries.
Perplexity Free hides which model answers (<cite index="29-2">Sonar auto-selected, no UI showing which variant</cite>), so quality is hard to compare like for like.

ui.platforms: Web (desktop browser) is best for a side-by-side recording. All four also have iOS and Android apps.
screens: UNVERIFIED FROM SEARCH, confirm in a live screen recording: all four are chat apps with a text box at the bottom or centre of an empty chat, a left sidebar with chat history and a 'New chat' button, and the account/profile at the bottom-left. Light or dark follows the system setting by default.
Gemini (verified): Settings is at the bottom left of gemini.google.com, and Usage limits opens from it. Chat activity is managed under Settings & help > Activity.
Perplexity: a search-style box with Pro Search/Research options. Answers show a numbered source list/citations (this is its signature; third-party sources confirm citations).
ChatGPT Free: a 'Think' button for harder questions (per OpenAI release notes). Free US users may see ads.
Claude Free: chat UI with Projects (up to 5 on Free), and a message when the 5-hour session limit is hit.
For the test screen: split-screen or four tiles with the same prompt pasted, and a scoreboard overlay (Research / Long writing / Coding / Content) with a winner badge per row.

research.visuals: A four-panel split screen with the identical prompt in each tool and the outputs side by side (research prompt: Perplexity's cited sources versus the others; coding prompt: the code blocks). Then a 4-row scorecard. A real screen recording of each tool is the only believable way to show the exact UI and answers. Don't fake answers, and show the results from your own run.
research.notes: Verdict is 'adjust'. The idea is valid: all four have free tiers and the test is real. But the source reel's claims (especially Gemini's free 'longest memory') are wrong, and the other tools it lists are out of scope. Limitations of this check: I did not reach official pricing pages directly, only OpenAI release notes, Anthropic and Google help-center snippets, plus third-party trackers. Several third-party pages use different model names (GPT-5.6 vs GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.x), so avoid naming models on screen. Re-check free limits on publish day (Perplexity 3 Pro Searches/day, ChatGPT 3 uploads/day, Gemini 32K). Suggested 'best for' framing is an opinion to be validated by the live test: Perplexity for cited research (verified: it shows sources), Claude for long writing (200K context on Free per third-party), Gemini for big-picture/Google-integrated tasks and images (verified features, but not for very long docs on Free), ChatGPT as the all-rounder with unlimited text chat. Coding and content winners are unverified, so let the test decide and say 'in my test'. Avoid saying 'forever free': these plans can change, and ChatGPT's changed twice in 2026.
